summary: A code-decided Not eligible on a rules-table card showed only the older code check's reason (e.g. 'Slate is an ineligible roof material regardless of age.') with no row and no quote; the table's own deciding row ([TWI-037] p.3) had been moved to diagnostics. Verdict unchanged. Fix: _code_owns_cards keeps the table's same-status rows and their quotes after the code's reason.
Harness false positive: the row-ID pattern [A-Z]{3}-NNN missed Progressive HO6's PH6-NNN IDs. Pattern widened; no product change.

Chubb's below-minimum Standard Tier referral is a code rule (Round 37, Liam's decision) quoting the guide ('Subject to pre-approval') without a row ID. The check now accepts a code decision that quotes the guide's sentence and does not hedge.

Step 7c (live Haiku sample, ~1 in 20 profiles) did not run: the session's permission classifier blocked reading the worktree .env with the API key ('Credential Leakage'). Not worked around. Spend $0. To run it, Liam can allow the live run (or run verification/fuzz with --live himself).
Harness false positive: 'Pool (in ground - unfenced, both slide and diving board entered): ...' states the answer; the re-ask patterns now skip the '(... entered)' part.

Second reader: Centauri DP3 lists 'Dwellings having unprotected swimming pools' under 'PROPERTY - Ineligible' (PDF p.5); the tool REFERS an Above Ground - Unfenced pool because CDP-053 is a CONDITION row (the cure, 'alternate approved enclosure', is not a form option). The card reads 'refers to underwriting: ... unprotected pools are ineligible', which contradicts itself. Same pattern on FOR-062, SLL-007, VDP-042 (CONDITION rows whose plain rule says ineligible). Liam: Refer (today) or Not eligible with a confirm note for the cure?

Second reader (twice): Chubb's secondary-home decline (primary not with Chubb) is right, but CHU-004's citation is always p.10 (the Dallas/Fort Worth / Northern table). Cameron (Coastal, p.12) and Montgomery (Austin/San Antonio/East/South, p.11) use other tables with the same footnote (county lists p.14). The reason's 'in the Standard tier' is narrower than the guide (Preferred has the same condition). Verdict unaffected; citation should follow the county group.

The card's first line (and Missing items) showed raw row IDs like '[PH6-074] declines: ...': cards._ROW and rules_evaluator._ROW_ID knew only three-letter prefixes, and Progressive HO6's rows are PH6-NNN. Both now take [A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2}-NNN. 20 of the first 100 batch-2 profiles.
hold_guard.ROW_ID is also [A-Z]{3}-NNN, so the hold guard does not recognise a row-cited PH6 item. Not changed: it decides holds, which can change a status. Same one-line widening if Liam agrees.

'Flat roofs are ineligible unless poured concrete' (CDP-023 Centauri DP3, PDP-099 Progressive DP3). Round 14's code check declines a flat roof with any discrete covering (shingle, tile, slate, metal); round 35's map audit made those a confirm. So Centauri declines with no row and no quote on the card, and Progressive DP3 gives a confirm for the same answers. A fix (237dfe4) was reverted: it changed Progressive DP3's verdict against round 35's deliberate test. Liam: is a flat roof with a shingle/tile/metal covering 'not poured concrete' (decline), or a confirm? Fixture centauri_flat_shingle_no_row and test_flat_roof_concrete are strict xfails.

Second reader UNCLEAR: Liberty HO3 Refer (2 losses in 5 years, PPC 10) is supported, but p.8's Ineligible list has three rules that may make it stricter and the card does not raise them: 'Dwelling located in a brush or wind hazard area' (undefined; profile is Tier 1 Jefferson County), 'Buildings owned by a corporation, company, LLC, etc.' (owner is an Estate), and 'Homes with Coverage A exceeding $1 Million in a Protection Class 10' (Coverage A blank). Ask Liberty/Safeco what 'wind hazard area' means; decide whether an estate counts.

Second reader, 5 of 20 verdicts (repeat): a decline's reason is the row's plain rule and never names the profile's value that fails it -- SAG-081/TRI-094 'Property must be in South Texas ...' without 'Wheeler/Tarrant County is not'; TRI-021/WIL ownership without 'Estate'; PH6-077 lists every roof type without 'wood shake'; NCD 'Stab Lok or Zinsco' without 'Federal Pacific panels are Stab-Lok'. Verdicts right. A general fix (name the failing answer, e.g. 'Roof: Wood shake / wood shingle -- ' before the rule) touches every card; left for Liam to choose the wording.

Estate ownership: Sage Trium / Wilshire decline it under 'other non-individual owned properties are ineligible' (estates not named; only family trusts excepted); Liberty HO3's 'Buildings owned by a corporation, company, LLC, etc.' may or may not cover an estate. Readers call the Sage reading literal but unconfirmed. Liam: confirm with SageSure / Safeco how an estate-titled home is treated.

Check 11: with PPC N/A and the station 5.9 miles away, Occidental DP3's held reason said it 'needs to know ... and station distance'. ODP-116's open-fact label is the fixed text 'station distance' (as on 8 other Sage/NatGen/Foremost fire-table rows); the open fact was the PPC. _open_fact_now drops a bare 'station distance' once the distance is given and names an unknown PPC; held_reason keeps the label's case. Status unchanged (still held: the PPC is open). Batch 3 (pre-fix code) hit it 12 times on 4 carriers; all re-checked clean on 67053b5.

Second reader: PRO-040 / PDP-087 / PH6-073 declined on the form's combined answer 'Federal Pacific or Zinsco panel', but Progressive names Federal Pacific only -- a Zinsco panel would not meet the rule. That answer alone is now a confirm ('the panel is Zinsco not Federal Pacific'), as FOR-041 already was. VERDICT CHANGE: a Progressive HO3/DP3/HO6 home whose only electrical flaw is that answer goes Not eligible -> Eligible (or whatever its other rows decide) with a confirm. The 22 other rows on that answer name both brands and still decline.

Second reader hour 3 (10 of 10 verdicts supported) noted confirms the card could add: HOAIC 'Risks older than 50 years require proof of updates' (1975 home); Swyfft 'More than 1 non-weather loss' with 2 losses of unknown type; Liberty trust ownership vs 'Buildings owned by a corporation, company, LLC, etc.'; NatGen Premier's closed-program citation has no page in the citation string (the reason has p.3); Chubb's citation page (F07) reproduced a third time (Duval -> p.11). Hour 5: ARI requires pools 'secured by a 6' high fence'; the form's fence box is 4 ft, so a ticked box does not settle ARI.

Same pattern as F15, for ownership: the form's 'Corporation / partnership' answer fails MER-005, but Mercury's guide (p.5) names 'an LLC, Corporation, and/or Corporate Trust' -- not partnerships. A partnership-owned home is an unproven decline. Not changed: round 35 step 3e (Liam's decision 1) cited MER-005 when the option was added. Proposed: 'Corporation / partnership' alone -> confirm 'the owner is a corporation, not a partnership'. Scanned all rows on the bundled answers: FOR-093 ('a business, including a corporation'), LIB-048 ('company ... or similar entity'), CHO-007 ('entity-named') and SLL-074 (LLP, refer) cover partnerships; LIB-028 / STD-041 (manufactured vs mobile) read as the same home type. Second reader hour 4 found the same with roofs: PRO-024 declines the form's 'Metal: corrugated / exposed-fastener / tin / aluminum panels' answer, but Progressive names only 'tin' and 'corrugated metal' (that option was grouped in round 35 step 3b, Liam's decision 1). Hour 5 (unclear): Progressive HO3 names only 'rubber membrane' while the form's 'Membrane (rubber/EPDM / TPO / modified bitumen)' bundles three; the card raised no roof item at all -- it should at least confirm which membrane.

Second reader WRONG_VERDICT: Chubb Not eligible on CHU-012 'Flat roofs are ineligible' for a Hip roof with a Built-up (tar and gravel) covering. The shared FLAT gate (build_rule_field_map.FLAT: roof_shape == Flat or roof_type in {Built-up, Membrane}) treats a built-up or membrane covering as a flat roof whatever the shape answer. The reader: should be Refer (Coverage A under $1M) with a confirm that the roof is not flat or low-slope. FLAT gates many carriers' flat-roof rows, so this is a design choice for Liam: let the shape answer win, or make the material-only case a confirm.

Second reader: PRO-012 declines a 'Corporate or business trust' as a business, but Progressive p.2 says 'Properties owned in the name of a trust or IRA must be referred to Underwriting' and names only a land trust as ineligible. Whether a business trust is 'a business' is not stated: Refer or a confirm, not a decline. (Verdict held on polybutylene and fuses in this profile.)
